summary: Orange County, Florida lookout named only in the Forest Lookouts listing; its 2008 auction sale for $1,500 is the one dated fact; no source describes the site now.

events.note: Sold at auction for $1,500, per the Forest Lookouts entry

corrections.proposed: no agency named in the source
corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts entry gives 'T20S-R27E-' as its only location detail beyond the county, which reads as a township and range (a land-survey location), not a managing agency.

evidence.supports: Only location detail on the entry beyond the county: township and range
Dated fact: tower sold at auction in 2008 for $1,500
evidence.quote: 2008: The tower sold at auction for $1500.00.

evidence.supports: Orange, Seminole and Brevard counties once had ten towers, now two
evidence.quote: In Orange, Seminole and Brevard counties there used to be ten; now there are only two.

evidence.supports: Towers phased out; cell phones let residents report fires from almost anywhere
evidence.quote: Lovett says the towers are being phased out, because in the age of the cell phones residents call in fires from almost anywhere.
Technology has taken over for manned fire towers and the towers themselves are being sold off.

sources.title: Fla. Fire Towers Being Sold Off

notes_for_editor: Confidence low. The only source that names this tower is the Forest Lookouts listing, which gives the county, a survey location (T20S-R27E-) and a 2008 auction sale for $1,500, and nothing else. The agency field in the current record holds that survey location, so the correction above proposes removing it; the editor should confirm the township-and-range reading before applying it. The 2010 WFTV counts (ten towers in Orange, Seminole and Brevard counties, now two) are county-group context and do not name this tower. Two searches turned up Massachusetts Plymouth towers, which are unrelated. The Plymouth, Florida Wikipedia article (read) mentions no fire tower. Neither the cached NHLR nor the cached FFLOS Florida index lists a Plymouth tower. Page reads: 3 (Plymouth listing, Firehouse article, Plymouth Wikipedia article).
